correctness.rationale: The published Rana--Parashar Section III asserts that g=∑(x_i²−x_i y_i) on nonnegative fixed-sum simplices minimizes at simultaneous uniform x,y. For fixed x, linear minimization in y puts its entire mass b on an argmax M of x. Holding M, Cauchy/convexity equalizes the other n−1 x coordinates, giving φ(M)=M²+(a−M)²/(n−1)−bM for M∈[a/n,a]. Its unconstrained optimizer (2a+(n−1)b)/(2n), clamped at a, proves the stated exact two-branch minimum for all n≥2,a,b≥0, including a=0 and b=0. Checked symbolically and by rational sample witnesses. Direct substitution of λ=(1,N/6,N/6,N/6,−N/4,−N/4), ξ=(1,0,0,0,0,0) meets the paper’s relaxed ordering/fixed sums/eigenvalue inequality and yields Eq (relaxed RHS)=−7N²/24 and discrepancy N(N−6)/48 versus claimed N(2−5N)/16 for 0<N≤1. The paper is right that relaxed spectra need not come from physical state/optimizer pairs; this correction does NOT overturn the actual physical counterexamples.
